title: How to Show a Gut Synapse

scenes.tts: In a mouse, light can silence one kind of cell in the lining of the gut. Then the mouse no longer reliably prefers sugar to a calorie-free sweetener. That cell is not a neuron. So how does it reach the nervous system? Through a hormone, or through a fast synapse onto a vagal neuron?
scenes.visual: A gut lining cell, silenced by light, weakens sugar preference; two unknown routes to a vagal neuron.
scenes.narration: In a mouse, light can silence one kind of cell in the lining of the gut. Then the mouse no longer reliably prefers sugar to a calorie-free sweetener. That cell is not a neuron. So how does it reach the nervous system? Through a hormone, or through a fast synapse onto a vagal neuron?

scenes.tts: Before 2018, the prevailing view was this, as Kaelberer and colleagues put it. The brain senses the gut only through passive hormone release. Then a process on enteroendocrine cells, once called a neuropod, was shown to touch mucosal nerves. Modified rabies virus was given by enema into the colon of newborn mice. It infected the cells and then labelled nerves. In two of five mice with infected colon nerves, labelling reached vagal nodose neurons. That shows connectivity. It does not show the transmitter.
scenes.visual: Hormone drifts off the cell; a process grows to touch a nerve; virus dots cross; 2 of 5 mice; transmitter still a question.
scenes.narration: Before 2018, the prevailing view was this, as Kaelberer and colleagues put it. The brain senses the gut only through passive hormone release. Then a process on enteroendocrine cells, once called a neuropod, was shown to touch mucosal nerves. Modified rabies virus was given by enema into the colon of newborn mice. It infected the cells and then labelled nerves. In two of five mice with infected colon nerves, labelling reached vagal nodose neurons. That shows connectivity. It does not show the transmitter.

scenes.tts: Next, speed. Researchers grew gut cells together with vagal neurons in a dish. Light switched on the gut cell. In nine pairs, currents appeared in the neuron within sixty to eight hundred milliseconds. The cells also carried transcripts for V G L U T one, which fits glutamate as the transmitter. Currents that fast point to a fast transmitter acting on the neuron.

Currents that fast point to a fast transmitter acting on the neuron.
scenes.visual: Pair in a dish; light on the gut cell; transmitter dots cross; neuron lamp on; timeline window 60 to 800 ms.

scenes.tts: Then a blocker. Kynurenic acid blocks ionotropic glutamate receptors. It abolished the currents. After washout, the currents came back. This was seen in four neurons. Recovery matters. It separates blocked receptors from damaged cells.
scenes.visual: Blocker bar on the neuron; current lamp off, then on after washout; blocked receptors vs damaged cells.
scenes.narration: Then a blocker. Kynurenic acid blocks ionotropic glutamate receptors. It abolished the currents. After washout, the currents came back. This was seen in four neurons. Recovery matters. It separates blocked receptors from damaged cells.

scenes.tts: Now the living mouse. In anaesthetised mice, a recording from the cervical vagus showed firing rise within seconds of sucrose in the intestine. Phloridzin, which blocks S G L T one, abolished that response. Light that silenced the C C K cells abolished it too. Light that drove the same cells raised vagal firing. The authors concluded that the cells are necessary and sufficient to transduce a glucose stimulus. Firing within seconds alone could fit a hormone or a synapse.

scenes.tts: All of this is mouse work, and each step has a limit. Tracing shows connectivity only. Cocultures are in a dish. Only eighteen point nine percent of C C K cells touched sensory fibres in fixed tissue. The human data are glutamate release from organoids of one donor. In a study of serotonin-making gut cells, the recorded fibres were not shown to be vagal. A synaptic route does not make hormones irrelevant. Keep the rule. A fast synapse is shown by a chain of evidence, not by one result.
